Revised assessment: The FOMC statement conveys a constructive macro backdrop—solid activity, strong labor markets, and inflation near 2%—supporting a 25 bp hike and guidance for “further gradual increases.” Operational choices (IOER set 5 bp below the top of the target range and use of ON RRP) align with maintaining control over the funds rate while balance-sheet runoff proceeds gradually.

Insights from the April 2018 SLOOS temper this positivity at the margin: banks reported wider loan rate spreads (a modest tightening in pricing), credit policies for commercial real estate loans changed with signs of tighter standards and softer demand, while residential real estate standards for qualified jumbo mortgages were largely unchanged; reports from foreign banks indicated activity/inquiries in C&I and CRE but not a clear acceleration. These survey readings point to mildly tighter bank credit conditions and mixed demand, introducing a small headwind that does not contradict the FOMC’s gradual hiking path but warrants a slightly less upbeat tone than otherwise.

Overall tone: positive fundamentals with measured tightening, modestly tempered by bank credit headwinds from SLOOS.
